design_principles: The documentary prompt is the primary input.
The factory dynamically generates research domains, questions, sub-questions, and search strategies.
Discovery, retrieval, evidence extraction, atomic claim extraction, corroboration, and script generation remain separate stages.
Metadata and abstracts are not treated as equivalent to full-text evidence.
Independent corroboration is based on independent works, not duplicate records.
The same DOI represents one independent scholarly work.
Uncertainty, disagreement, and research gaps are explicitly represented.
Visual evidence is a first-class research output.
All pipeline stages are restartable and idempotent.
Runtime storage is disposable; durable project state is preserved in the repository and structured registries.
No downloaded media is treated as authentic historical material merely because it exists online.
AI-generated imagery is a fallback/reconstruction asset and must never be silently presented as authentic archival material.

pipeline.name: research_planning
pipeline.purpose: Dynamically generate the research strategy from the documentary prompt.

pipeline.name: search_planning
pipeline.purpose: Generate question-specific search queries and source-type strategies.

pipeline.name: source_discovery
pipeline.purpose: Discover scholarly, institutional, archival, documentary, governmental, museum, and other relevant sources.

pipeline.name: visual_discovery
pipeline.purpose: Discover images, video, maps, diagrams, artifacts, documents, satellite imagery, historical illustrations, and other visual evidence relevant to questions and claims.

pipeline.name: source_normalization
pipeline.purpose: Normalize metadata, provenance, identifiers, versions, and source lineage.

pipeline.name: independence_analysis
pipeline.purpose: Determine which records represent the same underlying work or genuinely independent works.

pipeline.name: question_aware_ranking
pipeline.purpose: Rank sources according to research-question relevance, authority, evidence accessibility, independence, and documentary usefulness.

pipeline.name: targeted_retrieval
pipeline.purpose: Retrieve the strongest accessible evidence using source-appropriate routes such as HTML, PDF, repository, API, archive, or institutional page.

pipeline.name: evidence_extraction
pipeline.purpose: Extract source-grounded evidence with provenance and location information.

pipeline.name: atomic_claim_extraction
pipeline.purpose: Convert evidence into atomic propositions, with one independently assessable claim per record.

pipeline.name: claim_corroboration
pipeline.purpose: Test claims against genuinely independent works and identify agreement, disagreement, and evidentiary gaps.

pipeline.name: uncertainty_analysis
pipeline.purpose: Represent uncertainty, competing interpretations, causal limitations, chronology uncertainty, and unresolved questions.

pipeline.name: research_gap_detection
pipeline.purpose: Identify questions or claims that remain insufficiently supported and trigger additional research when necessary.

pipeline.name: verified_claim_ledger
pipeline.purpose: Create the final evidence-grounded claim registry used by downstream documentary generation.

visual_asset_model.purpose: Treat visual research as evidence and documentary planning data rather than a generic media bucket.

media_storage.purpose: Control disposable runtime storage without destroying research provenance.
cleanup_rules: Downloaded videos at least 7 days old are eligible for cleanup by default.
Never delete a video currently being processed.
Never delete a video explicitly marked preserved.
Never delete a video required by an active job.
Never delete final documentary outputs through this cleanup mechanism.
Never delete source metadata, provenance, evidence, claims, or licenses when deleting the local media file.
Record every deletion in a cleanup log.
Support dry-run cleanup before actual deletion.
Failed deletions must remain visible for later retry.

durability.runtime: Kaggle or other disposable execution environment

explicit_non_goals: Do not treat discovery metadata as evidence.
Do not call a claim verified merely because multiple API records repeat it.
Do not count Crossref and OpenAlex records with the same DOI as independent works.
Do not assume an environmental change proves civilization-wide collapse.
Do not assume a proposed decipherment of an undeciphered script is established fact.
Do not hard-code the Indus Valley topic into the reusable factory.
Do not silently present AI-generated reconstructions as authentic historical media.
Do not allow media cleanup to destroy provenance or evidence records.
